rationale: A coherent value × short-term cash-coverage conditional that is close to (but not identical with) the well-known Piotroski-style value-plus-financial-soundness combination, and the RANK([0,1]) × signed IND_ZSCORE construction means high B/M with negative coverage produces the most negative scores — an acceptable but worth-checking implementation of the intended conditioning.

The two legs are mechanically entangled (cash sits in `act`, so high cash mechanically depresses `lct/act`), making this largely a repackaged cash-to-price / current-ratio combination rather than an informative interaction.

Sales-to-price and leverage-change are each individually well-documented, but conditioning cheap revenue on a three-year deleveraging trend is a defensible value-trap screen with a hypothesis that matches the expression's direction.

Penalizing `dp/at` inside an EBITDA/EV signal is close to mechanically converting the ratio back toward the standard EBIT/EV multiple, so the "interaction" is largely a trivial redefinition of an already-published enterprise-multiple anomaly.

Value conditioned on working-capital stability is a reasonable and distinct construct, though the ABS operator discards the signed accrual information that the accrual anomaly says is the economically relevant part, weakening the stated "deteriorating fundamentals" rationale.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Gross-Margin Stability Sales Value signal — same value leg and same margin ratio with VOL swapped for TREND — and it offers no diagnosis of why that signal's FMB slope and FF5 alpha had opposite signs.
